title: Q2 两级调度：卡车跨区 + 三轮车区内
summary: R3 adds the integer rounding loss to the executable unmet one-for-one, as the review requires. The executable fixed point remains 975 tricycles with zero unassigned in all 50 zones, but the integer trips deliver 1,494.80 bicycles fewer than the LP flows (sum over zones of lp_bikes - int_bikes), so the executable unmet is 38,489.44 + 1,494.80 = 39,984.23, not 38,489.44. Recomputed: full-load convention layer cost 533,248.01, total 617,055.75, saving 902,223.20 (59.38%); actual-load plus deadhead mileage 1,873.59, layer 534,278.98, total 618,086.73, saving 901,192.22 (59.32%). Executable-basis break-evens become 1.47215 CNY per removed unmet trip and 1,225.36 CNY per tricycle-day. The sample zone 24 shows the same accounting: LP unmet 2,059.49 plus rounding 26.50 = 2,085.98. The cap-60 LP-layer result (889 tricycles, total 591,587.42, saving 61.06%) remains quoted only as the idealized bound whose own schedule leaves 534 of 13,775 trips unassigned. The paper must use the integer-execution plan: 975 tricycles, 617,056 CNY/day on the full-load convention, 59.38% saving (618,087 / 59.32% with actual-load mileage).

checks.3_city_executability: pass (finding, not pass/fail): at the priced 889, the city-wide integer schedule has 13,775 trips, 534 unassigned (3.88%) in 15 zones; the largest are zone 9 (135 of 3 tricycles), zone 29 (87 of 6), zone 21 (51 of 1). Blanket buffers at 1.05/1.10/1.15/1.20 give 959/1,003/1,045/1,088 tricycles but still leave 357/347/322/307 trips unassigned, so a percentage buffer is not the fix. Cause: the LP time coefficient 2d/(V Q)+2h/60 charges distance time per bicycle as if every trip carried Q bikes; partial-load integer trips cost 2d/V per trip, and the per-hour budget is exceeded. Evidence: schedule_check.json city and buffer_sweep.
checks.4_executable_fixed_point: pass; evidence=schedule_check.json exec_rows/exec_totals. The fleet is raised per zone until the LP at that fleet produces a trip list its own fleet can schedule; 15 zones were raised, the fixed point closes at 975 tricycles (+9.7%), zero unassigned in all 50 zones. The executable unmet must be measured on the integer trips, not the LP: sum over zones of (lp_bikes - int_bikes) = 1,494.80 bicycles are rounded away and each is one unmet departure at its sink (the LP equality is b_eq = resid, so one undelivered bicycle removes exactly one unit of service). Unmet: LP 38,489.44 + integer loss 1,494.80 = 39,984.23; removed 199,260.97. Full-load convention: vehicle-km 4,213.04, mileage 842.61, fixed 292,500, penalty 239,905.40, layer 533,248.01, total 617,055.75, saving 902,223.20 (59.385%). Actual-load+deadhead convention: 9,367.93 km, mileage 1,873.59, layer 534,278.98, total 618,086.73, saving 901,192.22 (59.317%). Difference 1,030.98 CNY/day (0.17% of total). Break-evens: penalty ceiling 1.47215 CNY per removed trip; fixed ceiling 1,225.36 CNY per tricycle-day. The fixed point uses the same greedy rule, so 975 is an upper bound on the executable fleet and 617,055.75 an upper bound on the executable cost; 59.38% is a lower bound on the saving.

notes: Integer unmet is not an estimate: each rounding loss is one undelivered bicycle at a sink whose LP constraint is an equality, so the LP unmet plus sum(lp_bikes - int_bikes) is the integer-execution unmet. Exact total 1,494.7969 at the 975-fleet; the review's 1,506 from bike-km/0.537 was a close estimate.

Cap 60 changes the LP optimum from 885 to 889 and removes the last capped zone (0 at cap). The gain is 691.37 CNY/day (0.12%); the R1 numbers are superseded everywhere. The sweep 20/25/30/40/60 is monotone in total cost, so no further cap increase is suggested.

The LP time budget is the root cause of the executability gap: t = 2d/(V Q) + 2h/60 charges the distance time per bicycle as if every trip were full, while the integer schedule charges 2d/V per trip. Partial loads therefore exceed the per-hour budget. The fixed point repairs this by raising the fleet, not by changing the cost model; a proper fix would put the integer trip count into the LP (a MILP or an iterative ceiling), which is out of scope here and is flagged for T021.

The fixed-point fleet 975 is an upper bound: it uses the same greedy earliest-finish rule, and a better assignment or a re-optimised allocation under the executable cost could lower it. Likewise 617,055.75 is an upper bound on the executable cost and 59.38% a lower bound on the saving.

The 10% blanket buffer arithmetic (974 for the old 885 fleet) is reported but not used: at 1.10 the per-zone buffer is 1,003 tricycles and 347 trips still go unassigned, because the failure is concentrated in a few zones with very small allocations (zone 21 has 1 priced tricycle and 51 unassigned; the fixed point raises it to 4).

Two unmet columns must be kept apart in the paper: LP-slack unmet 38,489.44 (the LP's own value after the fleet is raised) and integer-execution unmet 39,984.23 (adds the 1,494.80 rounding loss). The paper number is the latter. The same applies to zone 24: 2,059.49 LP vs 2,085.98 integer.

The global threshold 0.4311 CNY per removed trip is an LP-cost-model property (fleet scan with LP curves). On the integer-executable plan the threshold is 1.47215 and the fixed-cost ceiling 1,225.36; the paper should quote the latter and may mention 0.4311 only as the idealised bound.

N*(p) at cap 60: 203/457/580/731/889/1,340 for p=1/2/3/4/6/10. p=10 still has 3 zones at the cap, so 1,340 is a lower bound; the other rows are uncapped. Global LP-model threshold is unchanged at N=100 because no low-fleet allocation touches the cap.
